title: Methods of Psychology
summary: How psychology establishes knowledge: experimental, observation, case study, survey and correlational methods; strengths and limitations of each; correlation does not imply causation.

notes.t: Research methods are how psychology establishes knowledge. Each method trades off internal validity (cause–effect) against external validity (real-world generality).

r: Manipulates an independent variable, controls others, measures the effect
Systematic watching of behaviour in a natural or controlled setting
Observer bias; no control over variables
In-depth study of one individual or a small group
Rich detail; suited to rare cases
Questionnaires or interviews collecting self-report data
Measures the relationship between two variables without manipulation
Can study variables that cannot be manipulated

notes.t: The experimental method uses objective observation and experimentation as the basis for true knowledge. A worked example: Does sleep affect memory? The independent variable is sleep duration (manipulated), the dependent variable is memory performance (measured), and participant conditions and testing environment are controlled so any change in memory can be attributed to sleep duration.
Key warning: correlation does not imply causation — only the experimental design establishes cause–effect. Correlational research measures relationships between variables without manipulation.
